title: Tunisian knit stitch beanie
excerpt: A snug beanie that looks knitted but is worked entirely in Tunisian knit stitch on an aran weight yarn. Worked flat and seamed, it produces a classic v-stitch texture.
sourceNotes: Tunisian knit stitch inserts the hook through the front of the stitch rather than through the vertical bar, creating a v-stitch surface that resembles stocking stitch.

glossaryTerms.definition: A Tunisian stitch worked by inserting the hook through the centre of the v below the horizontal bar, drawing up a loop. The result mimics a knit stitch.
A flat joining method that draws the edges of two pieces together by weaving yarn through the edge stitches alternately, creating an almost invisible join.

crochet.gaugeText: 16 sts x 14 rows = 10 cm in Tunisian knit stitch on 5.0 mm hook.

Chain 88. Row 1 forward pass: pick up a loop in each chain (88 loops). Return pass: ch 1, work off 2 loops to end.
Forward pass: *insert hook through centre of next v-stitch, yarn over, draw up a loop; repeat from * across. Return pass as row 1. Work until the rectangle measures 22 cm.
Bind off with slip stitch across. Sew the short edges together using the tapestry needle and mattress seam to form the hat tube.
Thread a length of yarn through the tapestry needle. Run it through every stitch along one open edge, pull tight, and secure. Weave in all ends.
